chunks: Say: 'Verily my Lord increases or restricts the provision of any of His creatures as He will, and repays whatsoever you spend. He is the best of all providers.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's control over sustenance and spending?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Saba is often cited to highlight the divine wisdom behind the fluctuation of sustenance, linking material provision to spiritual testing and gratitude. It reinforces the concept of *al-Khaliq* (The Creator) as the ultimate source of all wealth, encouraging believers to view charitable expenditure not as a loss but as a divinely guaranteed investment. This assurance serves as a practical remedy for anxiety over poverty, grounding economic trust in God's attribute as *Khayr al-Raziqin* (the Best of Providers).
